Sofia —

Appreciate the clear ask. Quick answers up-front, then I included an attachment (finexia_cost_model_v2.xlsx) with the detailed calc and a short unit-econ summary below. Marissa and Vivek looped in to confirm the assumptions and update the MAP.

High level (hosted API):
- Tokens/month (your starting point): ~45,000,000 tokens/month = baseline for the POC.
- Effective tokens/$ (hosted): ~40,000 tokens per $1 at our standard text-generation pricing for the model family we demonstrated. That maps to ~$1,125/month raw token spend for 45M tokens (before caching/batching).
- Dedicated: price changes based on reserved capacity commit (flat monthly seat + reduced per-token when we hit sustained throughput). For budget prep, assume ~25% lower unit token cost if you commit to a Dedicated pool.
- Caching: With prefix caching for repeated account prompts and a conservative TTL (1h), our measured workloads saw a 20–35% reduction in total tokens. For your flows I recommend conservative 25% token reduction (we'll refine with traces).
- Batching: Default routing windows yield ~18–25% of requests batched at peak; with tuned client-side batching we can push that to ~40% on peak concurrency. Batching reduces compute overhead (lower latency per token and better throughput) but only marginally reduces billed tokens since billing is per output token. Biggest win is combining batching with caching to reduce total tokens emitted.

Unit-econ summary (baseline POC):
- Gross token cost (no caching): 45M tokens / 40k tok per $ = $1,125
- Expected caching reduction (25%): net tokens = 33.75M => $843
- Misc overhead (system prompts, eval telemetry): +8% tokens => ~36.45M => $911
- Hosted API estimate (rounded): ~$920/month for token usage during POC.
- Dedicated estimate (with 25% unit saving on tokens): ~$690/month equivalent token cost + monthly reserved capacity fee (TBD).

Next steps I propose:
1) Karaba team (Finexia) confirms the request distribution – average tokens/request and % repeated prefixes.
2) We instrument a 3-day trace capture in sandbox (we can do this by 2026-02-18) to validate cache hit rate and batching opportunities.
3) Update MAP to include the token assumptions, cache TTL, and a contingency item for Dedicated pricing if you move from POC to prod.

Attachments: finexia_cost_model_v2.xlsx (updated with the calculations above), Redwood_MAP_template_for_customer.pdf (internal).

If that works I'll update the MAP and push to the shared Drive link and to the HubSpot deal (link below).

Thanks — happy to sync live if needed.

Best,

Quick internal note on assumptions — agree with the approach but suggest we tighten a few items before sending to Procurement: 

1) Average tokens/request — Sofia's 250 tokens/request seems high if many responses are short. Ask for distribution: median vs mean. If median is 120, the saving is material.
2) Caching: recommend we specify two tiers in the MAP: 
   - Level A (prefix cache, TTL 1h): assume 25% hit rate => 20–25% token reduction (conservative)
   - Level B (session KV + identity hash, TTL 24h): only if Finexia opts into session caching; assume 40% hit rate => 30–35% reduction
3) Batching: important to call out that batching affects latency SLOs — include a note that we will target batching only where latency < 250ms impact. Assume conservative 20% batch rate by default for POC unless they accept 100ms extra p50.
4) Evals / safety telemetry: plan for +6–10% token overhead for logging and evals in POC; call this out as optional and show cost with/without telemetry.

Suggested MAP language additions (short bullets we can paste into Finexia_MAP_v2):
- POC token budget: 45M tokens monthly (baseline).
- Assumptions: avg tokens/request = 250 (customer to confirm), default cache TTL = 1h, expected cache hit = 25%, expected batch capture = 20%.
- Contingency: +/- 15% cost variance; monthly steering call to rebaseline.
- Decision point: Dedicated vs Hosted to be chosen before production rollout; Dedicated pricing requires 60-day lead time.

Risk to close timeline: Procurement may request a longer data retention SLA for logs; that may push Legal review by ~2 weeks. If we want to keep 2026-03-25 signature target, mark that as a close risk in the MAP and offer a 30-day trial credit to accelerate approval.

I'll edit the MAP draft and push to Drive. Vivek, can you validate the Dedicated savings assumption and the 60-day lead time?

—Marissa
Director, Solutions Engineering
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Sofia / procurement team —

Thanks for the patience. We've updated the MAP and cost workbook after an internal review; attaching Finexia_MAP_v1.pdf (annotated) and finexia_cost_model_v2.xlsx. Below is the concise summary you can share with Procurement / Legal.

Finalized POC assumptions (for MAP):
- Baseline traffic: 2,000 requests/day, target 3-week run; baseline avg tokens/request = 250 (customer to confirm with trace).
- Baseline gross tokens (no caching): 45,000,000 tokens/month.
- Hosted effective units: ~40,000 tokens per $1 => gross token cost ~$1,125/month.
- Expected cache hit (prefix cache, TTL 1h): 25% => net token spend ~$843/month.
- Telemetry & eval overhead: plan for +8% tokens => adjusted estimate ~$911/month.
- Recommended conservative estimate to put in the SOW: $920/month for token usage (rounded).
- Dedicated option: ~25% lower unit token cost after reserved commit; leads to ~$690/month equivalent token spend + reserved capacity fee (we will provide a committed-cost proposal if you want to scope Dedicated).

Batching note: default routing will batch ~20% of peak requests; if Finexia opts into a small client-side buffer (50–100ms) we can raise that to ~35–40% at peak. Batching primarily improves throughput and latency tail; it does not reduce billed output tokens significantly.

Close timeline and risks:
- Target contract signature: 2026-03-25.
- Known risks: extended Legal review for retention/SLA, Dedicated lead time (~60 days) if chosen, and higher-than-expected median tokens/request.
- Mitigation: 30-day trial credit + early sandbox trace capture to lock down cache hit rate.

Next steps:
1) Sofia: confirm whether you can provide a 7-day token trace or median tokens/request by 2026-02-18.
2) Karthik/Marissa: we'll push an updated MAP (Finexia_MAP_v2) with the bullets above to Drive and HubSpot.
3) Procurement: if you want a Dedicated pricing sketch, confirm expected monthly committed throughput and we'll produce a callout by 2026-02-21.

Attachments: Finexia_MAP_v1.pdf (annotated), finexia_cost_model_v2.xlsx (calc).
